title: Associativity, signed symmetry and units of scalar module cups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and $F,G,L$ arbitrary $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the $k$-bilinear scalar cohomology cups $H_k^p(X,F)\times H_k^q(X,G)\to H_k^{p+q}(X,F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}G)$ of [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], with tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $p,q,r\geq0$, $a\in H_k^p(X,F)$, $b\in H_k^q(X,G)$, and $c\in H_k^r(X,L)$. Under the canonical associator $(F\otimes G)\otimes L\cong F\otimes(G\otimes L)$, one has $(a\smile b)\smile c=a\smile(b\smile c)$. Under the canonical symmetry $\tau:F\otimes G\cong G\otimes F$, one has $\tau_*(a\smile b)=(-1)^{pq}b\smile a$. If $u_X\in H_k^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is the image of $1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ under the canonical degree-zero derived-sections comparison [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], then $(\lambda_F)_*(u_X\smile a)=a$ and $(\rho_F)_*(a\smile u_X)=a$ under the left and right tensor-unit isomorphisms. Coefficient isomorphisms act by the recorded cohomology functor. No quasi-coherence, separatedness, properness, or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0FP4 (lemma-cup-product-associative) and 0FP5 (lemma-cup-product-commutative), specialized to sheaves in degree zero; remark-cup-product and section-cup-product for the unit. For the scalar Yoneda convention, the sectionwise comparison has factor (-1)^(pq), whose associativity exponents satisfy pq+(p+q)r=qr+p(q+r).

proof.text: Write $a\star b$ for the ordinary unsigned module cup, with scalars restricted to $k$. Let $sF=F[0]$, $U=\mathcal O_X$, and $e=e_{-,n}$ be the normalized shifted-Hom equivalence. Put $B_{p,q}(f,g)=t_{p,q}\circ(f\otimes^{\mathbf L}g)$ and $d=(\lambda^D_{sU})^{-1}:sU\to sU\otimes^{\mathbf L}sU$. The comparison gives $e(a\star b)=m_{F,G}[p+q]\circ B_{p,q}(e(a),e(b))\circ d$, sends the canonical class of $1$ to $1_{sU}$, and sends coefficient maps to postcomposition. Its hypotheses hold for arbitrary module sheaves on the scheme $X$. The tensor-morphism calculus applies to the degree-zero source $U$: $U\otimes_{U}-$ is the identity, so $U$ is flat; no flatness of the target coefficients is needed.

source.place: Tag 0FP2, shifted-Hom construction and comparison to cup; coefficient and unit normalization

proof.text:
Expand the preceding formula twice for $(a\star b)\star c$. Naturality of tensoring and of $t$ moves the inner coefficient map $m_{F,G}$ to the target. After the ordinary coefficient associator, its target composite is
$$s(\alpha)\circ m_{F\otimes G,L}\circ(m_{F,G}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1).$$
For $a\star(b\star c)$ the target composite is $m_{F,G\otimes L}\circ(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}m_{G,L})\circ\alpha^D$. These are equal by augmentation coherence. The remaining shifted tensor maps are equal by associativity of $B$ in the cited calculus. The two source maps obtained by iterating $d$ agree under the source associator by the monoidal unit coherence axioms. Thus the two morphisms from $sU$ agree. Injectivity and coefficient naturality of $e$ prove ordinary-cup associativity under the stated coefficient associator.

source.place: Tag 0FP4; its tensor/counit associativity argument in shifted-Hom coordinates

proof.text: For ordinary symmetry, apply the coefficient map $s(\tau)[p+q]$ to the formula of step 1. The augmentation identity $s(\tau)\circ m_{F,G}=m_{G,F}\circ\sigma^D$ moves the symmetry before $m$. The shifted tensor calculus gives $\sigma^D[p+q]\circ B_{p,q}(f,g)=(-1)^{pq}B_{q,p}(g,f)\circ\sigma^D_{sU,sU}$. The symmetry on the tensor square of the unit fixes $d$, by the symmetric monoidal unit axioms. The resulting morphism is $(-1)^{pq}e(b\star a)$. Additivity, coefficient naturality and injectivity of $e$ give $\tau_*(a\star b)=(-1)^{pq}b\star a$. This supplies the sign argument omitted in the source's proof.

source.place: Tag 0FP5; omitted proof expanded using the Koszul shifted-tensor identity

proof.text:
The representative of $u_X$ is $1_{sU}$. In the left product its image after the coefficient unitor is
$$s(\lambda_F)[p]\circ m_{U,F}[p]\circ t_{0,p}\circ(1_{sU}\otimes^{\mathbf L} e(a))\circ d.$$
The augmentation unit identity replaces the first two factors by $\lambda^D_{sF}[p]$. The derived unitors are those of the fixed K-flat monoidal structure, descended from the unsigned module unitors on total tensor models. On total cochain models, $\lambda^D_{sF}[p]\circ t_{0,p}=\lambda^D_{sF[p]}$: the $U[0]$ factor has degree zero, so its shift-extraction sign is $(-1)^{p\cdot0}=1$. Unitor naturality then reduces the displayed map to $e(a)\circ\lambda^D_{sU}\circ d=e(a)$. On the right, use $s(\rho_F)m_{F,U}=\rho^D_{sF}$ and $t_{p,0}$, whose sign is identically one; right-unitor naturality reduces the map to $e(a)$. Left and right unitors agree on $sU$, so the same $d$ serves both computations. Injectivity of $e$ proves both ordinary unit identities in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0FKU, shifted-Hom construction with identity unit class; Tag 0FPB and the normalized total-tensor unitors

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon_{i,j}=(-1)^{ij}$. The signed scalar/module comparison gives $x\smile y=\epsilon_{i,j}(x\star y)$ for every coefficient pair and degrees $i,j$. All coefficient maps are the recorded additive cohomology maps, hence commute with these integer signs. Bilinearity yields
$$(a\smile b)\smile c=\epsilon_{p,q}\epsilon_{p+q,r}((a\star b)\star c),\qquad a\smile(b\smile c)=\epsilon_{q,r}\epsilon_{p,q+r}(a\star(b\star c)).$$
The two signs agree since $pq+(p+q)r=qr+p(q+r)$. For symmetry, $\tau_*(a\smile b)=\epsilon_{p,q}^2(b\star a)=b\star a$, while $\epsilon_{p,q}(b\smile a)=\epsilon_{p,q}\epsilon_{q,p}(b\star a)=b\star a$. Finally $\epsilon_{0,p}=\epsilon_{p,0}=1$, so both ordinary unit identities give exactly the stated scalar unit identities. No restriction on $X$ or its modules was introduced.
